    Genome Coverage of Topic Annotations in 0.01 cM Blocks

    annot_block_coverage.Rd

    For each topic annotation, the percentage of the genome's 0.01 centimorgan (cM) blocks that contain at least one annotated SNP. This is the size metric Tashman et al. (2021) use to decide when S-LDSC's block-jackknife p-values control type I error.

    annot_block_coverage(
  ldsc_res_dir,
  trait,
  nTopics,
  baseline_prefix,
  chrs = 1:22,
  block_cm = 0.01
)

    Arguments

    ldsc_res_dir

    Directory holding k*_output/annotations/<trait>/ for each topic, as produced by run_sldsc().

    trait

    Trait name used in the annotation filenames.

    nTopics

    Number of topics (K).

    baseline_prefix

    Prefix of the baseline annotation files (with CHR, BP, SNP, CM columns), matching the --ref-ld-chr of the S-LDSC runs.

    chrs

    Chromosomes to use. Defaults to 1:22.

    block_cm

    Block size in cM. Defaults to 0.01, as in Tashman et al.

    Value

    A data frame with one row per topic: topic, n_snps (reference SNPs in the annotation), prop_snps (as a fraction of all reference SNPs; note S-LDSC's Prop._SNPs counts MAF 5-50% SNPs only), n_blocks (blocks overlapped) and pct_blocks (percentage of the genome's blocks overlapped). The number of blocks in the genome is attached as attribute n_blocks_genome.

    Why blocks and not SNPs

    S-LDSC's significance tests rest on the block jackknife. For small annotations the jackknife standard error is noisy and correlated with the coefficient estimate, and the estimate itself is right-skewed, so very small p-values are inflated even when P = 0.05 is fine. The inflation depends on how many independent pieces of the genome an annotation touches, not only on how many SNPs it contains: 0.5% of SNPs packed into a few regions is far less reliable than the same number spread across the genome. The percentage of 0.01 cM blocks overlapped captures both size and clustering, and of six metrics compared it separated well- from badly-calibrated annotations best.

    In null simulations (3,750 phenotypes, 246 annotations) type I error was controlled for annotations covering at least 1.7% of 0.01 cM blocks for the one-sided test of the coefficient and the enrichment test (0.83% suffices for the enrichment test alone), and at least 8.3% for the two-sided test of the coefficient. All baseline-model annotations pass.

    Definition

    Blocks are floor(CM / block_cm) within each chromosome, using the genetic map positions (CM column) of the reference SNPs in the baseline annotation files. The genome's blocks are those containing at least one reference SNP; an annotation overlaps a block if any SNP in the block has a non-zero annotation value. The topic annotations must be thin annotations whose rows match the baseline files, as written by run_sldsc().

    References

    Tashman KC, Cui R, O'Connor LJ, Neale BM, Finucane HK (2021). Significance testing for small annotations in stratified LD-Score regression. medRxiv 2021.03.13.21249938.
